name: Wadsworth Atheneum
unique: The oldest public art museum in the country, with a castle facade, a Hudson River School collection, the first Picasso bought by an American museum and a baroque cabinet of curiosities.
buzz: The Morgan and the Hudson River rooms are the local favorites; the museum is quiet on weekday mornings and the café is in the old sculpture court.

name: Harriet Beecher Stowe Center
unique: The Victorian cottage where Stowe wrote after Uncle Tom's Cabin, kept with her desk, her paintings and a tour that connects the book to the present rather than treating it as a relic.
buzz: The guides are trained to run a conversation, not a lecture, and visitors say it is the most useful history tour in the city; Mark Twain's house is next door.

name: Elizabeth Park Rose Garden
unique: The oldest municipal rose garden in the country, with 15,000 bushes in a formal arbor and a pond, free and open at dawn.
buzz: Peak bloom is the third week of June and locals come before work; the park is safe and the greenhouses are open in winter.

name: Bushnell Park Carousel
unique: A 1914 Stein and Goldstein carousel with 48 hand carved horses and a Wurlitzer organ, still turning in a glass pavilion in the middle of downtown.
buzz: A two dollar ride that adults take without children; the park around it is the oldest public park in the country.

name: Yale University Art Gallery
unique: The oldest college art museum in the western hemisphere, with a Van Gogh, a Trumbull revolution cycle and a room of African art, all free.
buzz: The Trumbull paintings and the modern galleries are the route; it is free and rarely crowded on weekday afternoons.

name: Yale Center for British Art
unique: Louis Kahn's last building, a four story box of oak, linen and concrete holding the largest collection of British art outside Britain, including Constable and Turner.
buzz: The building is as good as the paintings and the long gallery on the top floor is the place to sit; admission is free.

name: Grove Street Cemetery
customer: History walkers, architecture fans, Yale visitors
unique: The first chartered cemetery in the country, laid out in family plots on a grid with an Egyptian revival gate, holding Eli Whitney, Noah Webster and Lyman Beecher.
buzz: The gate and the Whitney monument are the landmarks; it is a quiet walk between Yale and the Hill and free maps are at the entrance.

name: East Rock Park
unique: A traprock ridge with a carriage road to a soldiers' monument and a cliff view over New Haven harbor, plus a trail down to the Mill River.
buzz: The summit is a 20 minute walk and the view of the city and Long Island Sound is the payoff; the road is closed to cars in winter.

name: Peabody Museum
unique: A natural history museum with a brontosaurus mount that helped start the dinosaur craze, a great hall of mammals and an Egyptian collection, reopened after a major renovation.
buzz: The dinosaur hall is the reason children ask to return; admission is free and the new galleries are brighter than the old ones.

name: Weir Farm National Historical Park
unique: The farm where American impressionist J. Alden Weir painted for 40 years, with his studio, a pond and a trail where the park supplies easels and paint.
buzz: Artists can borrow supplies and paint on the grounds; the studio tour is short and the property is the only national park devoted to painting.

name: Maritime Aquarium
unique: A aquarium built in a 19th century ironworks on the Norwalk River, with a shark tank, seals and a research vessel that takes people out on Long Island Sound.
buzz: The touch tanks and the seal feeding are the hits; the harbor cruise is the add on and the building itself is a nice piece of industrial reuse.

name: Beardsley Zoo
unique: The state's only zoo, with a New England farmyard, a carousel and animals from the Americas, in a park designed by Frederick Law Olmsted's firm.
buzz: The farmyard and the tigers are the route with small children; it is small enough to finish in two hours and the parking is free.

name: Sherwood Island State Park
unique: The first state park in Connecticut, 238 acres of beach and salt marsh on Long Island Sound with a nature center and a September 11 memorial garden.
buzz: The beach is wide and the parking is the only cost; the marsh boardwalk is quiet and good for birds at low tide.

name: Mystic Aquarium
unique: A beluga whale habitat, a penguin pavilion and a touch tank of sharks, next to Mystic Seaport so a family can do both in a day.
buzz: The belugas and the sea lion show are the draw; buy the combined ticket with the seaport and arrive at opening.

name: Ocean Beach Park
unique: A half mile of beach with a 1940s boardwalk, a carousel, a bandshell and a bathhouse that still looks like a seaside postcard.
buzz: The boardwalk and the ice cream stand are the tradition; parking is the cost and the beach is calm and shallow.

name: Harkness Memorial State Park
unique: A 42 room Roman renaissance mansion on a Long Island Sound point with a formal garden, a pergola and a lawn that runs to the water.
buzz: The gardens and the mansion terrace are the photo backdrop; the house is only open on tour dates and the beach is rocky.

name: Eugene O'Neill Theater Center
unique: The campus where new American plays and musicals are workshopped before Broadway, with a barn theater, a mansion and readings that cost a fraction of a city ticket.
buzz: Audiences see shows in development and are asked for feedback; the summer season is short and the grounds are open to walk.

name: Lime Rock Park
unique: A 1.5 mile road course in the Berkshire foothills where spectators can walk the paddock, sit on the hill at the uphill and watch vintage cars race without a grandstand ticket.
buzz: The Labor Day vintage festival is the weekend to go; the track is small, the access is unmatched and the loudest cars are the point.

name: Kent Falls State Park
unique: A quarter mile of cascades dropping 250 feet over marble ledges, with a trail alongside and a covered bridge at the bottom.
buzz: The climb is short and steep and the upper pools are the quiet part; in spring the water is loud and in August it is a trickle.

name: American Mural Project
customer: Art people, families, labor history fans
unique: The largest indoor collaborative mural in the country, 120 feet long and five stories high, filling a former textile mill with painted tributes to American workers.
buzz: Visitors are unprepared for the scale; you can walk into parts of the mural and the mill building is part of the exhibit.

name: White Memorial Conservation Center
unique: Four thousand acres of woods, ponds and boardwalks around a small nature museum with live owls and a working weather station.
buzz: The boardwalk and the owls are good with children; the trails are flat and the museum is small enough for an hour.

name: Nathan Hale Homestead
unique: The Hale family farmhouse where the 21 year old schoolteacher who said he had only one life to give grew up, with period rooms and a heritage breed farm.
buzz: The house tour ties the famous last words to a real family; the grounds and the farmers market in summer are free.

name: Stafford Motor Speedway
unique: A half mile oval that runs Friday night short track racing under lights, with modifieds, late models and a grandstand where you can see the whole track.
buzz: Friday night races are cheap and loud and the modified division is the local obsession; bring a jacket, the hill is cold after dark.

name: Mansfield Drive-In
unique: A three screen drive-in in the woods where you tune the radio, sit on the tailgate and watch two features for the price of one.
buzz: The snack bar is cash only and the double features are the deal; arrive early for a good spot and bring bug spray.

name: Roseland Cottage
unique: A Gothic revival summer cottage painted bubblegum pink, with original 1850s wallpaper, a boxwood parterre garden and a bowling alley in the carriage house.
buzz: The color and the bowling alley are the surprises; the tour is short and the garden is free to walk.

name: Air Line Trail
unique: A 50 mile gravel rail trail on the old Air Line route, crossing stone arch bridges and a gorge on the Natchaug River.
buzz: The Thompson to Putnam section and the Willimantic bridge are the highlights; the surface is gravel and better on a hybrid than a road bike.

name: Thompson Speedway Motorsports Park
unique: A five eighths mile oval plus a road course on the same property, one of the oldest closed circuit tracks in New England, with open track days for street cars.
buzz: The road course track days are the way in for drivers; the oval races are cheap and the grandstand is old school.

name: Connecticut River Museum
customer: Boat people, history families, river walkers
unique: A museum in a 1878 steamboat warehouse on the river, with a working shipyard, a 1906 schooner and the story of the Connecticut's shipbuilding trade.
buzz: The schooner sails in summer and the museum is small; combine it with the Essex steam train across town.

name: Hammonasset Beach State Park
unique: Two miles of beach on Long Island Sound with a boardwalk, a campground in the pines and the Meigs Point nature center at the eastern end.
buzz: The park is huge and the west beach is the family side; the nature center has live animals and the campground books early.

name: Devil's Hopyard State Park
unique: Eighty foot Chapman Falls drops into a pothole marked gorge on the Eightmile River, with trails through hemlock and a legend about the devil that the park does not endorse.
buzz: The falls are a five minute walk and the orange trail climbs above them; it is small and popular on summer weekends.
